results.title: Rewrite the need before naming tools
results.conclusion: The coherent target is an owned, evidence-conditioned decision; tool names are not part of its success condition.

results.title: Build the hammer and its genuine opposite
results.conclusion: Opposition is useful when it changes the intervention mechanism and retains the same outcome; this run does not establish a universal winning workflow.

results.title: Investigate the layers before choosing a remedy
results.conclusion: The real cross-layer defects concern incomplete obligations and evidence-stage ambiguity; passing structure and untested effectiveness are compatible claims.

results.title: Reverse the order: distill, then challenge, then repair
results.conclusion: A ranked proposal list is too small: it loses decision ownership, evidence boundaries, and reopening conditions.

results.title: Run an intervention-family tournament
results.conclusion: Preserve a conditional portfolio: evidence generation, decision rules/ownership, and removal/direct action. The matched method arms produced no selection winner.

results.title: Solve a tiny case with the hammer unavailable
results.conclusion: A direct source inspection can solve the bounded evidence-warrant question without the incumbent workflow; its transfer boundary is narrow.

results.title: Test the causal fork
results.conclusion: On these synthetic cases, discriminating evidence changed justified actionability; added process structure did not change choices at fixed evidence.

results.title: Attack failure residue rather than the happy path
results.conclusion: The residue worth preserving is a usable, source-linked decision state even when a helper, owner, or evidence path fails.

results.title: Borrow a mechanism through an explicit bridge
results.conclusion: Borrow the eligibility mechanism from admission control; keep quantitative queue claims conditional on the stipulated model.

results.title: Compare the human need with the machine representation
results.conclusion: The local human/machine checklist lost evidence and explicit success-measure coverage; a complete obligation comparison detects that loss.

results.title: Compare construction value with operating burden
results.conclusion: Choose among methods using context-specific benefit and support burden; this run supports no universal Pareto winner.

results.title: Make removal, reuse, and delegation selectable exits
results.conclusion: Reuse decisive evidence and remove redundant obligations where the required outcome survives; keep all explicitly requested strategy coverage.

results.title: Alternate building and reframing with a hard budget
results.conclusion: Bounded alternation improved the decision unit; continued repetition without new evidence would add terminology rather than resolve uncertainty.

results.title: Give the method itself an applicability and expiry test
results.conclusion: Direct inspection is adequate for the explicit field-membership and evidence-warrant questions; causal efficacy questions require more evidence.

results.title: Invert the assumption to open another mechanism
results.conclusion: Typed inversion opens hypotheses while formal entailment checks stop inverse/converse errors and constraint-violating reversals.

results.title: Attack with the goal of expanding the design space
results.conclusion: An attack becomes useful when it exposes a changeable assumption and yields a testable opening; invalid attacks and hard constraints must also close honestly.
